parts.title: The History of the Pencil
parts.article:
The History of the Pencil V2

(A) Pencils have existed for millennia. It is known that the ancient Egyptians, Greeks and Romans all used small pieces of metal as writing instruments, and that 14th-century European artists made pale grey drawings with thin rods of lead, silver or zinc. It is, however, generally accepted that the history of the modern pencil began in the 16th century, in the hilly, rural county of Cumberland in north-west England.

(B) Some time before 1565, an enormous deposit of the soft, dark grey mineral now known as graphite was discovered in the Borrowdale district of the county. Then, as now, Cumberland was a farming area, and the locals found the mineral useful for marking their sheep so they could identify the ones that belonged to them. It was thought to be a form of lead, and so was referred to as plumbago, a term deriving from the Latin name for that element. However, the mineral was later identified as a form of carbon, and in 1789 the German geologist Abraham Gottlob Werner renamed it graphite, a word based on the ancient Greek grapho, meaning ‘draw’ or ‘write’.

(C) The graphite found at Borrowdale was extremely dense and it could easily be sawn into sticks to be used for marking, writing or drawing. But because graphite is also soft, it requires some form of encasement around it, and so the sticks were initially wrapped in string for stability and ease of use. The news of the usefulness of these early pencils spread far and wide, attracting the attention of artists throughout Europe.

(D) In England, the government soon realised the value of the Borrowdale find, particularly for national defence purposes, because graphite proved ideal for lining the moulds used in the making of cannon balls. The mines were therefore taken over by the government, which guarded and periodically flooded them to prevent theft. Because of this, there were occasions when supplies for use in pencils had to be smuggled out in secret. Nevertheless, England still became the centre of a thriving pencil-making industry.

(E) Although deposits of graphite existed in other parts of the world, they were not of the same exceptional purity and quality as Borrowdale graphite, and had to be crushed to a powder to get rid of the impurities. England therefore continued to enjoy a monopoly on the production of pencils until a method of reconstituting the graphite powder could be found. English pencils continued to be made with sticks cut from pure Borrowdale graphite into the 1860s, after which the design was modified. The town of Keswick, close to the Cumberland graphite find, still manufactures pencils today, the factory also being the location of the Cumberland pencil museum

(F) Experimentation in pencil production was widespread across Europe during the 16th and 17th centuries. Around 1560, an Italian couple named Simonio and Lyndiana Bernacotti made what are probably the first blueprints for the modern, wood-encased pencil. Their concept involved the hollowing out of a stick of juniper wood, and placing a stick of graphite inside. Shortly thereafter, a superior technique to that of the Bernacottis was adopted: two wooden halves were carved, a graphite stick inserted, and the halves then glued together — essentially the same method in use to this day.

(G) The first attempt to manufacture graphite sticks from powdered graphite was in Nuremberg, Germany, in 1662, using a mixture of graphite together with the elements sulphur and antimony.

(H) Today, pencils are manufactured around the world, using graphite from a number of sources. Most manufacturers use a mix of graphite and clay as the core of their pencils. Each of these substances is ground into a fine powder, which goes on to be cleaned in order to remove any impurities. After the two types of powders have been dried, they are mixed together using water. The amount of clay added to the mixture depends on how hard the pencil is intended to be — higher proportions of clay will make the pencil harder — and the amount of time spent grinding the mixture determines the quality of the core. The graphite-clay mixture is then shaped into long sticks, and after drying these are heated in a kiln to 1,200°C. In the next step in the process, the graphite-clay sticks are immersed in melted wax, which is absorbed into the mixture and helps to make it write more smoothly. In the next stage, the manufacturers use thin planks of cedar wood or juniper wood. Several long parallel grooves are cut into the planks, and the graphite-clay sticks are inserted into these. A second plank which has been prepared in the same way is then glued on top. The whole assembly is then cut into separate pencils. The outside may then be varnished, retaining the natural colour of the wood, or painted in different colours.

analyses.content: 题目限定只能填一个词，原文明确说是标记羊（sheep），你不要错填成农场（farming）。
Then, as now, Cumberland was a farming area, and the locals found the mineral useful for marking their sheep so they could identify the ones that belonged to them.
原文说当地的农民用这种矿物给羊做记号来辨认归属，所以填 sheep。
原文提到当时人们以为这种矿物是一种铅（a form of lead），所以填 lead。
你可能想填 plumbago，但那是后来“被称为”的名字，题目问的是“最初被认为是一种什么”。
It was thought to be a form of lead, and so was referred to as plumbago, a term deriving from the Latin name for that element.
原文说英国政府（the government）很快意识到了这个发现的价值，特别是用来造炮弹，所以填 government。
注意字数限制只能填一个词，你直接填核心名词 government 即可，不要把前面的 English 也写进去。

In England, the government soon realised the value of the Borrowdale find, particularly for national defence purposes, because graphite proved ideal for lining the moulds used in the making of cannon balls.

questions.question: Borrowdale graphite was superior to all other forms of graphite.

analyses.content: 你不要看到“世界其他地方也有石墨”就选 FALSE，重点是后半句在强调质量上的绝对优势。
原文明确说世界其他地方的石墨在纯度和质量上都比不上 Borrowdale 的石墨，说明它是最好的，因此选 TRUE。

Although deposits of graphite existed in other parts of the world, they were not of the same exceptional purity and quality as Borrowdale graphite, and had to be crushed to a powder to get rid of the impurities.

questions.question: Pencil production in the Borrowdale area only lasted until the 1860s.

analyses.content: 原文说1860年代后只是修改了设计，并且紧接着说当地至今仍在制造铅笔（still manufactures pencils today），所以“只持续到1860年代”是错的，选 FALSE。
你可能会被1860s这个时间点骗到，但紧接着下一句就推翻了停产的说法，做判断题一定要看完整段语义。

English pencils continued to be made with sticks cut from pure Borrowdale graphite into the 1860s, after which the design was modified. The town of Keswick, close to the Cumberland graphite find, still manufactures pencils today, the factory also being the location of the Cumberland pencil museum

questions.question: The Cumberland pencil museum contains examples of pencils from different European countries.

analyses.content: 原文只提到了这家工厂也是 Cumberland 铅笔博物馆的所在地，完全没提里面有没有展览欧洲其他国家的铅笔，所以选 NOT GIVEN。
脑补是做阅读的大忌，不管博物馆里理应有什么，文章没提到的事情千万不要自己去猜。
The town of Keswick, close to the Cumberland graphite find, still manufactures pencils today, the factory also being the location of the Cumberland pencil museum

questions.question: A technique which improved on the Bernacottis’ method of making pencils is still used now.

analyses.content: Shortly thereafter, a superior technique to that of the Bernacottis was adopted: two wooden halves were carved, a graphite stick inserted, and the halves then glued together — essentially the same method in use to this day.
原文的 superior 对应题目的 improve，in use to this day 对应 still used now，你不要因为换了词就不敢选。
原文说后来采用了一种比 Bernacottis 夫妇更高级（superior）的技术，而且这个方法至今仍在使用（to this day），和题目完全一致，选 TRUE。

questions.question: In 1662, manufacturers in Nuremberg made pencils with graphite imported from England.

analyses.content: 原文确实提到了1662年德国纽伦堡在造铅笔，但根本没说他们的石墨是不是从英国进口的，所以选 NOT GIVEN。
题目里有具体的年份和地点很容易让你觉得是 TRUE，但只要核心信息（imported/进口）没提到，就必须选 NOT GIVEN。
The first attempt to manufacture graphite sticks from powdered graphite was in Nuremberg, Germany, in 1662, using a mixture of graphite together with the elements sulphur and antimony.

analyses.content: 原文说磨成粉之后会去清理（cleaned）杂质，然后才晾干（dried），所以填 cleaned。
题目问的是粉碎之后、晾干之前做了什么，原文是用 which goes on to be cleaned 表达了这个过程，你不要填成后面的 impurities（杂质）。

Each of these substances is ground into a fine powder, which goes on to be cleaned in order to remove any impurities. After the two types of powders have been dried, they are mixed together using water.
The graphite-clay mixture is then shaped into long sticks, and after drying these are heated in a kiln to 1,200°C.
原文说混合物做成长条并在晾干（after drying）后，会被加热（heated）到1200度，所以填 heated。
你可能想填 kiln（窑），但题目要填的是一个和 dried 结构并列的被动动作，所以必须填 heated。
原文说长条接着被浸泡（immersed，对应题目的 dipped）在融化的蜡（wax）里，所以填 wax。
你可能会在原文死找 dipped 这个词，但只要发现原文把它替换成了 immersed，紧跟着的名词 wax 就是答案。
In the next step in the process, the graphite-clay sticks are immersed in melted wax, which is absorbed into the mixture and helps to make it write more smoothly.
原文说木板上刻了平行的凹槽（grooves），然后把长条塞进这些凹槽里，因此填 grooves。
题目问的是放进木板里的什么地方，原文其实是用代词 these 指代了前面的 grooves，顺藤摸瓜往前看一眼就能找到。
Several long parallel grooves are cut into the planks, and the graphite-clay sticks are inserted into these.
原文说到铅笔外层可能会被上清漆（varnished）或者涂上不同颜色的漆（painted），所以填 varnished。
题目有个很明显的“or painted”，原文一模一样也是“varnished... or painted”，找到 or 就能锁定前一个词。
The outside may then be varnished, retaining the natural colour of the wood, or painted in different colours.
